mainTopic: How many people must be present for a declaration of הפקר (making something ownerless) to work, and the closing of the פרק אין בין המודר
overview: On the previous amud the גמרא found two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other about הפקר. One says an item leaves its owner as soon as he declares it ownerless. The other says it stays his until someone else takes it. This amud opens with a second answer: it depends on how many people heard the declaration. Before three people it is real הפקר, and before two it is not. This follows רבי יוחנן quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק. רבי יהושע בן לוי disagrees: by Torah law even one person is enough, and the חכמים asked for three only so that one can take the item and two can testify. The פרק אין בין המודר then ends with the הדרן.

steps.title: Second answer: two listeners versus three listeners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the contradiction between the two ברייתות. One speaks about a declaration made before two people, and the other about a declaration made before three.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it this way: the ברייתא that says the item stays with the owner speaks about someone who declared it ownerless in front of two people. The ברייתא that says it becomes ownerless right away speaks about someone who declared it in front of three people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to explain why the two ברייתות seem to disagree about הפקר. It says they are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the two ברייתות looked like they disagreed about the law of הפקר itself. This answer says they do not argue at all. Each one describes a different situation, decided by how many people heard the declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces another possible answer
Ownerless property that anyone may take
In front of, in the presence of

phrases.english: That one is where he declared it ownerless before two people,
phrases.notes: "That one" is the ברייתא saying the item stays with the owner until someone else takes it.

phrases.english: and this one is where he declared it ownerless before three people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the contradiction between the ברייתות raised on the previous amud
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא describes a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות truly disagree about whether הפקר works right away
steps.terutzMaskana: Both can be true: three listeners make it הפקר right away, and two listeners do not

steps.title: Source: רבי יוחנן says three listeners are required
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source for the split between two and three listeners. רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, says a declaration before three is הפקר, and one before two is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: anyone who declares something ownerless in front of three people, it is ownerless. In front of two people, it is not ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the answer in the last step is not invented. It is based on a known rule from an אמורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer needed someone to say that the number of listeners matters. רבי יוחנן's rule says exactly that: three works and two does not. This fits the two ברייתות neatly.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who declares something ownerless

phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמַּפְקִיר בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה — הָוֵי הֶפְקֵר,
phrases.english: Anyone who declares something ownerless before three people, it is ownerless;
before two people, it is not ownerless.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the two-versus-three answer
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the ברייתות split between two listeners and three listeners
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: three makes it הפקר, two does not

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: by Torah law one listener is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds that by Torah law a declaration of הפקר works even before one person. The חכמים asked for three only so that one can take the item and two can be witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: by Torah law, even in front of one person it is ownerless. So why did the חכמים say three? So that one person can take it and two can testify.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different view of why three people are mentioned. For him, the number is about proof, not about whether the הפקר works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, three people are needed for the הפקר to work at all. For רבי יהושע בן לוי, הפקר works by Torah law even with one person. The rule of three is only a practical step: one person takes the item, and two can later testify that it was declared ownerless and that he took it.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on הפקר. רבי יוחנן: three listeners are needed for it to work at all. רבי יהושע בן לוי: by Torah law even one is enough, and three is asked for only so that one can take the item and two can testify.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהושע בן לוי says a declaration before fewer than three people is meaningless. In his view the הפקר works by Torah law. Three is only a way to have proof.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה אֲפִילּוּ בְּאֶחָד — הָוֵי הֶפְקֵר,
phrases.english: By Torah law, even before one person, it is ownerless;
and what is the reason they said three?
phrases.notes: "They" means the חכמים who made the rule of three.

phrases.english: So that one will take possession

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן about why three listeners are mentioned
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By Torah law הפקר works even before one person. Three is required only so that one can take the item and two can serve as witnesses.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic question in the laws of הפקר: is the number of listeners part of what makes הפקר work, or is it only a way to have proof?

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אין בין המודר
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing formula for the פרק called אין בין המודר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק אין בין המודר.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק ends here. The learner says the הדרן, a promise to come back and learn this פרק again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the chapter. Whatever comes next will begin a new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: said when finishing a פרק
The name of the פרק being completed

phrases.english: We will return to you, "There is no difference between one who is prohibited by vow"
phrases.notes: A פרק is named by the first words of its opening משנה, so this is just the chapter's name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion of הפקר
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק אין בין המודר
